text:
ellie: emergency WFH thread: my ISP cut the line during streetworks and the only place with steady signal is the laundry chute (yes really). photo: https://imgur.com/a/laundry-chute-router (1 pic)
ellie: pro tip: don't put the router on top of a pile of clean socks unless you like lint in the vents. :sweat_smile:
raghu: iconic. is it at least sheltered from the dryer heat?
ellie: it's in the chute chamber, so cool but echo-y. had to snake a short Cat6 through the door gap and zip-tie it to the chute handle. high drama.
nora: that sounds hilarious. duct tape or cable clips?
ellie: combo. duct tape for temporary show-stopping, clips for the final 12 hours.
devops-bot: Reminder: file an ISP outage ticket if latency > 100ms or packet loss > 0.5%. Use /ispsupport to escalate.
ellie: filed ticket #78765. support said a crew's scheduled tomorrow. in the meantime i tethered a backup LTE hotspot (thanks, old phone).
tyler: numbers? curious if hotspot is usable for calls.
ellie: ran a ping and a quick speed check while on a call: 
```
$ ping -c 5 8.8.8.8
PING 8.8.8.8 (8.8.8.8): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=0 ttl=116 time=48.1 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=1 ttl=116 time=51.2 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=2 ttl=116 time=49.0 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=3 ttl=116 time=47.6 ms
64 bytes from 8.8.8.8: icmp_seq=4 ttl=116 time=50.0 ms
--- 8.8.8.8 ping statistics ---
5 packets transmitted, 5 packets received, 0% packet loss
avg = 49.2 ms
```
ellie: decent for audio + screen-share, but no multi-person video.
raghu: poll: best temporary router hideout you've used? 1) Attic crawlspace 2) Laundry chute 3) Kitchen pantry 4) Under the stairs
nora: 4 for me, spiders are the gatekeepers.
tyler: 1 once, zero regrets but lots of insulation.
ellie: 2 for now. will move back upstairs after the crew comes by.
devops-bot: Need a loaner power strip or cable? Use /hardware-request.
ellie: requested a short patch cable and an inline surge. thanks bot.
raghu: pls post a final selfie with the chute router. it's for science and morale. :camera_with_flash:
ellie: will share an aftermath photo if the router survives the lint invasion. also labeling cable "DO NOT UNPLUG - ELLIE'S LIFE" for housemate clarity.
nora: mandatory housemate sticker. +1 for labeling.
ellie: thanks team, moral support is appreciated. also, anyone want the abridged how-to for stealth Cat6 routing? i'll write it up if people are into it.
raghu: yes please, bless the future you.
